chunks: He said: I found in an old manuscript written in Ahwaz in Muharram of the year 317 AH: Abu Abdillah said: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ismail ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib al-Jurjani narrated to us, saying: I was in the city of Qom when a discussion arose among our companions regarding a man who had disowned his son. They sent a man to the Sheikh (may God preserve him). I was present with him (may God support him). The messenger handed him the letter, but he did not read it and ordered him to go to Abu Abdillah al-Bazufari (may God glorify him) to answer regarding the letter. So he went to him while I was present. Abu Abdillah said to him: 'The boy is his son, and he had intercourse with his mother on such and such day in such and such place. Tell him: Let him name his son Muhammad.' The messenger returned to the city, and they recognized the truth, and the matter was clarified for them. The son was born and named Muhammad.

key_terms.الْبَزُوفِرِيِّ: Al-Bazufari, a title/name of the recipient

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) confirm the paternity of a disowned child in the Book of Ghayba?
ai.summary: This epistle from the Book of Ghayba illustrates the Imam’s use of precise, verifiable signs (burhan) to resolve a specific dispute over paternity in Qom, demonstrating the continuity of his authority during the Minor and Major Ghayba. By commanding the child be named Muhammad, the Imam not only confirmed the lineage but also linked the family to the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the spiritual and social cohesion of the Shia community under his guidance.
